description: Well-lit, centered, looking at camera (the reference)
notes: Baseline. signalState == ok, framing in dead zone, gazeOnCamera == true. Every other clip is a deviation from this one.
High backlightDelta (backgroundLuma - faceLuma). Should not be misread as lowConfidence unless faceLuma is low enough to actually impair detection.

description: Single lamp hard from one side
notes: Expect elevated clippedHighlightFraction and/or clippedShadowFraction on one side; framing/state otherwise ok.
Low faceLuma and backgroundLuma. This is the 'too dark to detect a face' case (§6.1) which MUST be distinguishable from noFace.
distanceError > 0, large interocularDistance relative to Config.defaults.targetFraming.interocularWidth.
distanceError < 0, small interocularDistance relative to target.

MUST produce error.x < 0 and instruction 'right' under both MirrorState.mirrored and MirrorState.notMirrored capture configuration. This is the spec §3.4 MUST-have test; see EgocentricTransformTests for the unit-level version of this invariant.
Symmetric case to clip 7: error.x > 0 and instruction 'left', both mirror configurations.
error.y > 0 (subject above target); likely also partially out of frame at the chin.
error.y < 0 (subject below target).

description: Looking down at a second monitor
notes: gazeOnCamera == false via pitch magnitude (chin down); framing itself may be fine.
gazeOnCamera == false via yaw magnitude.
Elevated |roll| in FaceGeometry; should not itself be conflated with yaw-driven gaze-off-camera.

faceCount briefly > 1; primary face selection and framing for the primary subject must remain stable through the transient. Suppression/hysteresis should prevent a spurious announcement for a brief background transit.
faceCount == 2 sustained; requires the .multiFace capability path. Priority ladder (§7.4) determines what, if anything, is announced about the second person.
Elevated clippedHighlightFraction localized near the eyes; watch for spurious lowConfidence if glare confuses landmark/quality detection.
Near-uniform frame -> high frameLumaVariance suppression (low variance). Own message per §6.1, distinct from noFace and lowConfidence.
Frame-level suppression (§7.2): blink state / N-consecutive-frame requirement must prevent any announcement from a normal blink or fidget.
Brief occlusion/interference must be absorbed by the N-frame requirement (§7.2) and 800ms dwell (§7.1); no face-lost escalation should trigger.

description: Subject leaves frame entirely and returns
notes: Exercises the full §7.3 escalation ladder (silence 0-1.5s, earcon at 1.5s, speech at ~5s) and, if absence is long enough, the userLikelyAway stop at ~30s plus the single 'Back, centered'-style recovery announcement on reacquisition.
